A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IncEventGS. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and references are readable and support comparison, including v3's supplementary material. v1 contains no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original Replica simulations, TUM-VIE evaluations, novel-view synthesis and trajectory results, and initialization/window-size ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds Gaussian-method comparisons, fast-motion and color-event evaluations, and efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: Supplementary Section 9 adds Bayer-filtered event and SSIM losses for color inputs and a ground-truth-pose training variant. The core Gaussian representation, trajectory interpolation, tracking/mapping, and depth-based bootstrapping already appear in v1; the expanded initialization description does not establish a new initialization procedure.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates grayscale indoor scenes from Replica and TUM-VIE. v3 retains these and adds color object reconstruction on the EventNeRF dataset, including lego, materials, drums, chair, and ficus, plus a fast-motion/blur comparison on Replica (Sections 8–9, Figures 6–7). These substantially extend domain and test-scenario coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds ESVO2 to TUM-VIE pose evaluation, E2GS* and EvGGS to Replica reconstruction comparisons, and MonoGS/SplaTAM to fast-motion comparisons. It removes E2VID + DEVO + 3DGS from Table 1 and Figures 2–3, while retaining standalone DEVO in Table 2.

E3.justification: The original data generation, reconstruction/trajectory metrics, hyperparameters, and optimization budgets remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce E2GS without blurred-image supervision, pretrained EvGGS evaluation, known-versus-estimated-pose controls for color reconstruction, and timing/storage measurements. These extend the protocols without revising the established main experiments; fast-motion settings remain sparsely specified.

E4.justification: The depth-initialization and event-window ablations in Tables 3–4 are retained unchanged. v3 adds qualitative fast-motion robustness comparisons, a color-reconstruction comparison with versus without ground-truth poses, and computational-efficiency analysis. These examine additional robustness, pose-dependence, and resource-cost questions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional average efficiency figures do not document a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Shared numerical entries in Tables 1–4 are unchanged. v3 adds ESVO2 errors, Gaussian-baseline scores, efficiency measurements, and fast-motion/color findings; it also revises real-data renderings and removes E2VID + DEVO + 3DGS results. New Table 6 shows mixed rankings: on room2, IncEventGS exceeds E2GS* in PSNR but trails in SSIM (0.79 versus 0.82) and LPIPS (0.23 versus 0.20).

T1.justification: v3 corrects the projected covariance dimension from 3×3 to 2×2 and introduces Bayer-filtered loss definitions in Equations 16–17. Equations 12–13 also omit v1's explicit window averaging, although implementation consequences are unspecified. These are limited mathematical revisions; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly claims the event-specific initialization strategy as a novel main contribution, replacing v1's separate efficient-rendering contribution bullet. The central claims of pose-free incremental Gaussian reconstruction and superior reconstruction/trajectory accuracy remain.

C2.justification: The supplement adds explanations concerning EvGGS's generalization to unseen data and pose-estimation difficulty on feature-poor objects. It also discusses remaining artifacts, optimizer-related efficiency limitations, and possible second-order optimization. These add applicability qualifications without substantially changing interpretations of the retained experiments.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the camera pose used for depth-based re-initialization, identifies PyTorch/Adam, and reports training time, storage, rendering speed, and approximately 0.3/1.7 seconds per chunk for tracking/mapping. Main hardware, hyperparameters, iteration budgets, and repository access remain unchanged. These are primarily additional disclosures.

R1.justification: v3 adds E2GS, ESVO2, MBA-SLAM, BAD-NeRF, and BAD-Gaussians references and associated positioning or attribution. It removes the Plenoxels and Instant-NGP background discussion. The principal distinction from known-pose event reconstruction and frame-based SLAM remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 polishes grammar and event terminology, rewrites some explanations, separates initialization into Section 3.5, and moves ablations before quantitative/qualitative evaluation. It adds supplementary sections, an author, and acknowledgements, while retaining the main narrative structure.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout, with substantial figure/table resizing and relocation. v3 adds Figures 5–7 and Tables 5–6, changes comparator rows in existing displays, and refreshes several real-data reconstruction panels. The original pipeline and trajectory visualizations are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 provides more relevant Gaussian-method comparisons and makes computational costs assessable, improving empirical support and transparency. However, the new fast-motion/color tests remain mainly qualitative and sparsely specified, and Table 6's broad superiority statement overlooks E2GS* advantages on several SSIM/LPIPS entries. These weaknesses temper the useful gains, supporting a limited overall improvement.
